summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require unsubscribe facilities in political electronic messages and require actors in electoral telephone calls to be identified at the start of the call.
Electronic messages containing federal electoral matter and having an Australian link would need clear opt-out instructions and an electronic address operating for at least 30 days.
The rules would apply to messages and calls sent after commencement on the day after royal assent, with exceptions for government and charity communications added to the unsubscribe rules.
changes: Failure to meet the new electoral message unsubscribe requirements would attract civil penalties under spam legislation.
Political parties' commercial messages would need an unsubscribe facility to qualify for the designated message exemption.
The unsubscribe address would have to handle reasonable traffic throughout the day during its required operating period.
summary.affected: Voters, political parties, candidates, other electoral message senders and campaign actors would be affected.
